indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap about the abbreviation for America
wandering letters stray out of order, so the word president is to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreary head of state rambles aimlessly about the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges PRESIDENT into PEDESTRIN, and 'around' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means plodding and unimaginative, a synonym of dull.

parts.note: china plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means a pal

indicators.note: a word's finish is its final letter, so only the end of plate is taken

explanation.surface: Delicate porcelain crockery has a pale glaze.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate', so china = PAL; 'plate's finish' is E. The surface shows the full slang phrase, then splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pale and light both describe a colour with little depth, as in light blue or pale blue.

clue.text: Party, American, owning rage is treacherous

indicators.note: owning means having something within, so the party word holds the synonym for rage

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
rage and anger are synonyms
US is short for American, as in US politics

explanation.surface: A political party with an angry American member is described as untrustworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: A treacherous road or situation is hazardous, which is what dangerous means.

clue.text: Simultaneous artillery launches, very offensive initially

definitions.text: Simultaneous artillery launches, very offensive initially

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Guns all firing together make a highly aggressive opening.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the first letters of its five words spell the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of guns fired at the same moment, describing exactly such an attack.

clue.text: Managed company with pure naked malice

parts.note: ran a business means managed it

indicators.note: naked strips the outer covering, so the word pure loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone ran a firm out of nothing but spite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips pure to UR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep-seated bitterness or ill will, close in sense to malice.

clue.text: Adult more serious about married suitor

parts.note: A is the film-certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: about says the word for more serious goes round the abbreviation for married

parts.note: direr, more dire, means more serious

explanation.surface: A grown-up, rather grave, courts a wedded partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M inside DIRER, giving DMIRER after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor is someone who courts another, an admirer seeking their affection.

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the capital's name is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy, a foreign capital to a British setter

explanation.surface: A trip abroad to a capital city, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: ROME and ROAM sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander or journey widely, a form of travelling.

indicators.note: collars means grips or encloses, so the phrase holds the answer inside it

explanation.surface: A police officer in the TV drama Endeavour arrests a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: Endeavour is a British TV detective series about the young Inspector Morse. The answer sits inside cOP IN Endeavour; 'suspect' is the verb, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion, which is to suspect or suppose something.

clue.text: Target's aim somehow to find justice

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An archer's goal is somehow to see fair play done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'justice' here is a title, as in Justice of the Peace, not the abstract idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A magistrate is a judicial officer, and a justice of the peace is a type of magistrate.

clue.text: Almost go before gold one plunders

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to predate something is to come before it in time
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Nearly first in line for gold, someone goes looting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts PREDATE to PREDAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A predator preys on others, such as a looter who plunders.

clue.text: Animal fat all in on spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so these letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: Animal fat is smeared all over something, like butter on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a noun for a butter-like paste but signals rearranging ALL IN ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the grease from sheep's wool, a fatty substance from an animal.

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A monarch harms someone, leaving them bruised.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking means leaving a mark, and a bruise is one kind of mark; the question mark shows that it is only an example.

indicators.note: disgusting describes a messed-up state, telling us to jumble the letters

explanation.surface: A filthy toilet is cleaned with bleach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgusting' rearranges LOO CURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To decolour is to remove colour, which is what bleaching does.

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so the doctor letters enclose the abbreviation for say

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, plus the S of the possessive
eg (for example) is a way of saying 'say'

explanation.surface: A doctor is keeping something that's left over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is a stock signal for an example, hence the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs are the sediment or last remnants left at the bottom, so they are what remains.

parts.note: suggests someone delaying a railway train, but the train is the long trailing part of a wedding dress

explanation.surface: A railway worker is delaying a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding up' sounds like delaying, but here it means lifting; the train is on a bride's gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride and may carry her dress's train down the aisle.

parts.note: seems to be about a bird spotted by other birds, the crows, but crows is a verb: this bird is known by its call

explanation.surface: A bird gets recognised by a flock of black corvids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crows' looks like a plural noun for the black birds; read it as the dawn cry instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a male farmyard cockerel, famous for crowing at daybreak.

parts.note: suggests paraphernalia for making cigarettes of cannabis, but the joints are cuts of meat turned over a fire

explanation.surface: Kit for making cannabis cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: A joint is also a large cut of meat to roast.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit is a rotating rod or device that turns meat as it roasts over a fire.

indicators.note: either way says the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: a thing which turns round an axis is named by the noun formed from the verb rotate

explanation.surface: A muscle that can twist in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome, so it 'turns' and still reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is a muscle that rotates a limb or part of the body, as in the rotator cuff.

indicators.note: changing tells us to alter the order of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Someone switching partners announces their sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges PARTNERS I.
explanation.definitionFit: When facts transpire they become known or emerge, which is what coming out means.

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing in a box, so the title word goes round the aristocrat word

parts.note: a deed is a document of title to property, the title deed
Sir is the style of a knight or baronet, here loosely an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A championship belt is fought over by a nobleman eager for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' suggests a sporting crown; here it is the legal title to property.
explanation.definitionFit: Desired is the past tense of desire, which means wanted, as coveted does.

clue.text: Possibly last round of French drink

parts.note: de is French for of
cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Perhaps the final round of drinks, in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' suggests drinks bought for a group; here it is a stage in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is a game or round that settles a contest, often the last one.

clue.text: Sharp matron bustling round ward, finally

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go round the letter taken from ward
bustling means moving about busily, so the word matron gets mixed up
finally picks out the last letter of ward

explanation.surface: A curt senior nurse hurries about the hospital ward at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bustling' rearranges MATRON and 'round' puts it around D, the end of ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is biting and caustic, a sense also carried by sharp.

parts.note: ilk means type or kind
so as an intensifier means very or terribly, as in so tired
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A kind of man who is extremely timid.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, timid man, the kind of meek male who keeps very quiet.

clue.text: Mops with sailor on board ship

indicators.note: on board means being inside a vessel, so these letters are placed inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A deckhand cleans the decks of a vessel with a mop.
explanation.definitionFit: Swabs are mops used to clean a ship's deck, and to swab is to mop.

clue.text: A politician's top friend creates outrage

indicators.note: a word's top is its first letter, so the start of politician is taken

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A politician's best friend causes a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' takes P from politician. 'top friend' looks like best friend; here 'top' works only on politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to shock or horrify, which is to outrage someone.

clue.text: Finish pass with sweetheart swallowing drinks

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something in, so the drink word goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
the heart of sweet is its middle letter, a crossword convention
laps means drinks as a cat does

explanation.surface: A football move ends with a final pass after someone's partner downs drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finish' is a verb here: to finish up exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse is to fall down or fail, so it can mean to finish exhausted or come to an end.

parts.note: a world map in its most detailed form is a full book of maps

explanation.surface: A finished map of the globe is very detailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a bound collection of maps, a fuller version of a single world chart.

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the bachelors letters go round the queen letter

parts.note: BAs are Bachelors of Arts
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Graduates hug the monarch's backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts R inside BAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bras are undergarments that support the breasts, hence supporters.

parts.note: TikTok is an example of an app, hence the 'perhaps'
lied means told falsehoods, fabricated a story

explanation.surface: A social media video was faked, or was it genuine?
explanation.definitionFit: Applied science or maths is put to practical use in real situations, rather than kept theoretical.

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the joining word takes in the letter for one

parts.note: to solder is to join metal using melted alloy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Signing up lets in a hired gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts I inside SOLDER. The question mark shows that a mercenary is just one kind of fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercenary is a soldier who fights for pay, so it is an example of the answer.

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or fiddle them

indicators.note: regularly ignored drops every other letter of clue, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: Welfare fraud happens when the hint is consistently disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops C and U from clue, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: The dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit.

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the papers word goes round the party word

parts.note: the press means the newspapers
a posse is a group or party of people

explanation.surface: Biased newspapers cover a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepossess is to influence someone in advance, to prejudice or bias them.
